objective: Give generated companions meaningful personal combat identities and specialisations, build composed procedural enemy encounters with clear counterplay and thematic persistent rewards, then research and implement broader encounter-design improvements while preserving open exploration and completing tooling/native verification.

requirements.description: Measure fresh-expedition recruitment, travel/discovery, combat and recovery across seeds with real runtime paths and explicit audit limitations.
Generate persistent combat traits and meaningful authored choices for all four classes with real effects, no-cost rejection, exact saves and mouse-accessible readable choices.
Ordinary generated worlds contain composed support, preparation/disruption and attrition groups with fixed transparent intentions, contextual placement and meaningful counterplay.
Encounter risk and identity drive themed supplies/equipment and distinctive boss rewards, with one-time persistent ownership and no save or retreat reroll exploits.
After initial implementation, research Slay the Spire, Caves of Qud and comparable games using primary sources, document findings and implement and verify the adopted encounter-generation rules.
Retain open dungeon access, fixed world threats, generated companions, mouse input, paused turn-based combat, shared rules, collision/privacy, deterministic RNG and safe persistence.
Each new family has validated IDs/references/schema/scaffolding/safe editing and real previews; recurring debugging tasks become reusable agent tools and documentation.
Full fresh tests and native scenarios pass with inspected minimum-size captures, project/verification documentation and a requirement-by-requirement completion audit.
